title: The Allure 2
content:
The chicken wing clamped between Lan Jingyi’s teeth slipped free. It landed in his bowl with a dull plop, splattering thick, brown sauce across the pristine white of his collar.

One overwhelming thought echoed through Wei Wuxian’s skull: The second he sobers up, Lan Wangji can never show his face in public again.

Jin Ling’s eyes darted between them, caught in sheer, bewildered horror. "...What the hell is he doing?"

Wei Wuxian cleared his throat, improvising smoothly. "Demonstrating an alternative use for the Lan clan forehead ribbon."

Lan Sizhui blinked, completely lost. "An... alternative use?"

"Naturally," Wei Wuxian explained without skipping a beat. "Suppose you encounter a particularly stubborn, peculiar walking corpse in the wild, and you decide it needs to be hauled back to the sect for further examination. In a pinch, you can untie your ribbon and truss it up like this to tow it along."

Jingyi’s voice cracked in outrage. "How could that ever be allowed?! Our clan ribbon is meant to—"

Lan Sizhui reached out, grabbed the dropped chicken wing, and shoved it straight back into Jingyi’s open mouth. "I see!" Sizhui declared with wide-eyed conviction. "To think our sacred ribbon possessed such marvelous utility! How truly enlightened!"

Ignoring the utterly bizarre looks shooting at them from every corner of the tavern, Lan Wangji kept a firm grip on the ribbon lead and dragged Wei Wuxian straight up the stairs.

Cross the threshold. Turn. Shut the door. Drop the latch.

And as the final touch, Lan Wangji shoved a heavy wooden table flush against the doorframe, barring the entrance as though sealing out an invading army.

Watching him fuss through all this frantic busywork, Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "What's the plan here, Hanguang-jun? Chopping up a corpse?"

The private suite was divided by an ornate standing screen. One side held a low dining table and cushions for entertaining guests, while the other housed a long daybed draped with delicate curtains for resting. Lan Wangji hauled him past the painted divider, gave him a solid shove, and sent Wei Wuxian tumbling flat across the cushions.

The daybed was backed by a heavy wooden headboard, and Wei Wuxian’s skull knocked against the timber with a dull thud. Just to be dramatic, he let out a theatrical yelp: "Ow!"

Internally, he couldn't help but sigh. Don't tell me he's forcing me into bed with him again? It's not even nine yet!

Hearing the cry, Lan Wangji gave the hem of his white robes an elegant flick and settled serenely onto the edge of the mattress. Reaching out a pale hand, he stroked Wei Wuxian’s head with impossible gentleness. Even with his face completely devoid of expression, the tenderness of the touch was unmistakable, silently asking: Does it hurt?

Beneath the soft petting, Wei Wuxian’s lips gave a violent twitch. "It hurts!" he whined, turning on the charm. "It hurts so bad, Lan Zhan, it's killing me!"

Hearing the barrage of complaints, a faint trace of worry clouded Lan Wangji’s brow. His petting softened even further, his hand drifting down to give Wei Wuxian’s shoulder a slow, consoling pat.

Seizing the opening, Wei Wuxian thrust his bound wrists into the man's face. "Then let me go! Look at this, Hanguang-jun—you tied it so tight my hands are about to fall off! It stings like hell. Be a good boy, untie the knot, and let me loose, yeah? Please?"

Lan Wangji’s hand shot out and clamped firmly over his mouth.

Wei Wuxian’s eyes widened. "Mmph! Mmm-mph, mmm-mmm-mmph?!"

You selectively deaf hypocrite! If you don't like what I'm saying, you pretend not to hear—and when you can't even fake that, you just gag me outright?!

The sheer audacity!

Fine, Wei Wuxian thought, narrowing his eyes. You brought this on yourself.

With Lan Wangji’s palm pressed flush against his lips, Wei Wuxian parted his mouth just a sliver, darted out the very tip of his tongue, and lightly flicked the center of Lan Wangji’s palm.

It was barely a feather-light brush, but Lan Wangji recoiled as though a lick of raw fire had scorched his flesh, yanking his hand back instantly.

Wei Wuxian drew in a deep, triumphant breath of air, reveling in his petty revenge—only to see Lan Wangji spin around, turning his back entirely. Curled up at the far end of the mattress, Lan Wangji pulled his knees tight to his chest, cradling the licked hand against his heart like a wounded dove, frozen stiff.

Wei Wuxian blinked. "Hey... what’s with the melodrama?"

The sheer, devastated posture looked like a maiden who had just been dishonored by a shameless rogue. Anyone walking in would think Wei Wuxian had committed some unspeakable crime against him!

Seeing him looking so deeply shaken, Wei Wuxian teased, "Hated it that much? Well, you asked for it—who told you to be so bossy and shut me up? Come here, let me wipe it clean for you."

Holding up his tied wrists, he reached out toward Lan Wangji’s shoulder, only for the man to lean away with a swift, agile dodge. Watching the great Hanguang-jun huddled in the corner of the bed, knees hugged to his chest, the urge to cause pure chaos detonated in Wei Wuxian’s chest.

Dropping to his knees on the blankets, Wei Wuxian crawled closer, letting loose his most wicked, villainous purr: "What's the matter? Scared?"

Lan Wangji practically vaulted off the daybed. Acting genuinely spooked, he kept his back turned, retreating across the room to put distance between them.

Now Wei Wuxian was having the time of his life.

He swung his legs off the bed, leisurely stalking forward with an impish grin. "Oh? Why run? Don't run away! My hands are tied and I'm not running, so what are you sweating for? Come on, come back here~"

Chuckling with shameless mischief, he closed in. Lan Wangji slipped past the folding screen, only to get boxed in by the heavy table he’d wedged against the front door. The second Wei Wuxian rounded the partition to corner him, Lan Wangji darted around the opposite side.

They looped around the screen like a pair of mischievous children. After seven or eight laps, right at the peak of the thrill, a sudden wave of sanity struck Wei Wuxian like cold water.

Wait... what the hell am I doing?

Are we seriously playing hide-and-seek right now?!

Did my brain get crushed in a doorframe? Lan Zhan is plastered out of his mind, but why am I playing along like a toddler?!

Noticing his pursuer had frozen in place, Lan Wangji stopped dead in his tracks too.

Tucked safely behind the wooden screen, he slowly poked half of his snow-white face around the edge, silently peeking out at Wei Wuxian.

Wei Wuxian stared back. The man’s expression was pristine, solemn, and impeccably dignified—looking for all the world as if the six-year-old playing tag around the furniture a second ago was a completely different person.

Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "Want to keep going?"

Lan Wangji gave a slow, deadpan nod.

Wei Wuxian choked, biting the inside of his cheek so hard he nearly sustained internal bleeding.

Lord have mercy... The peerless Hanguang-jun gets drunk, and the first thing on his agenda is playing hide-and-seek!

A tsunami of helpless laughter roared through his chest. He shook from head to toe, struggling to keep a straight face. Right. Raised under the Lan clan's four thousand rules—no shouting, no fooling around, not even allowed to walk briskly. He probably never got to run wild once as a kid. What a pitiful little life. Well, he won't remember a single thing once he sobers up anyway. Might as well indulge him.

Putting on a menacing swagger, Wei Wuxian took two stomping strides forward. Sure enough, Lan Wangji bolted again.

Treating it like babysitting an oversized toddler, Wei Wuxian chased him around the room for two more laps, shouting playful threats: "Run, run! Better run fast! If I catch you, I'm licking you again—see if you dare!"

He’d intended it purely as a mock threat.

Instead, Lan Wangji abruptly rounded the corner of the screen and marched straight into him, colliding chest-to-chest.

Wei Wuxian had been bracing to give chase; caught entirely off guard by his quarry delivering himself on a silver platter, his hands hovered uselessly in the air. Seeing him hesitate, Lan Wangji took the initiative. Grabbing Wei Wuxian’s bound wrists, he looped both of the man's arms over his own shoulders, effectively trapping his neck in a willing noose.

Lan Wangji looked him dead in the eye and declared, "Caught."

Wei Wuxian blinked. "...Uh? Right. Caught."

Lan Wangji lingered in the embrace, as if waiting for something with quiet anticipation. When nothing happened, he repeated the word, his voice dropping heavy, laced with an impatient, urgent nudge:

"Caught."

Wei Wuxian stammered, "Yeah, I heard you... caught."

Caught. And then?

What had he just promised? If I catch you, I’m going to—

...No way.

Wei Wuxian cleared his throat, trying to backpedal. "Wait, this doesn't count. You walked straight into me yourself—"

Before the excuse left his mouth, Lan Wangji’s face plummeted into a thunderous scowl, pure winter frost coating his features in raw displeasure.

Wei Wuxian was genuinely flabbergasted. Are you serious? Getting drunk doesn't just turn him into a kid playing tag—he actually likes being licked?!

He tried to lift his arms from Lan Wangji’s neck, but Lan Wangji clamped down on his forearms, pinning them against his shoulders with unyielding strength.

Looking at the pale hand resting on his sleeve, Wei Wuxian hesitated. Leaning his face down, his lips ghosted across the cool skin of Lan Wangji’s knuckles in a half-kiss, the tip of his tongue lightly brushing the back of his hand.

Just a feather-light, teasing flick.

Like lightning, Lan Wangji snatched his hand back, shoved Wei Wuxian’s arms away, and bounded across the room. Huddled against the plaster wall, he cradled his hand against his ribs, staring down at the floorboards in stubborn, blushing silence.

Wei Wuxian scratched his cheek, thoroughly stumped. Is he terrified, or does he like it? Or is he terrified of how much he likes it?

While he was turning the riddle over in his mind, Lan Wangji turned around, his face smoothing back into icy composure.

"Again."

Wei Wuxian choked. "Again?! Again what?!"

Lan Wangji slipped back behind the screen, poking half his face out to peer at him.

The message was painfully clear: Again. You chase, I run.

Speechless, Wei Wuxian gave in. He took two steps forward, and true to form, Lan Wangji threw himself right into his arms on beat two.

"You're definitely doing this on purpose," Wei Wuxian deadpanned.

Lan Wangji looped Wei Wuxian’s arms around his neck once more, wearing an expression of pure, innocent incomprehension, patiently waiting for his prize.

Why should he get to have all the fun while I do all the work? Wei Wuxian thought, a wicked grin spreading across his face. Whatever I do to him now, he'll have zero memory of by dawn. Time to raise the stakes.

Keeping his arms looped around Lan Wangji’s neck, he guided them both down onto the daybed.

"You really enjoy this, don't you?" Wei Wuxian murmured, leaning in close. "Don't turn your head away. Answer me: do you like it or not? If you like it this much, you don't need to waste time playing tag first. I'll give you your fill all at once."

Reaching out, he took Lan Wangji’s slender, porcelain hand, bowed his head, and pressed a soft kiss between his long fingers.

Lan Wangji instinctively tried to pull back, but Wei Wuxian held fast, refusing to yield an inch.

Drifting upward, Wei Wuxian’s lips brushed across the distinct ridges of his knuckles, his warm breath trailing a path of fire along the skin to the back of his hand. Right there, he pressed a second, lingering kiss.

Unable to break the grip, Lan Wangji curled his fingers tight, his hand trembling into a fist.

Tugging the pristine white sleeve back just an inch, Wei Wuxian exposed the pale curve of his wrist—and pressed another kiss against the pulse point.

He didn't lift his head. Peeking up through his eyelashes, he murmured, "Had enough yet?"

Lan Wangji’s lips remained pressed in a stubborn, unyielding line.

Wei Wuxian straightened up slowly, his voice dropping into an interrogation. "Tell me the truth: did you ever burn spirit money for me?"

Silence.

Wei Wuxian chuckled softly, leaning in until his chest brushed the other man's robes, pressing a kiss right over Lan Wangji’s heart. "Keep quiet and you don't get any more. Speak: how did you recognize me?"

Lan Wangji’s eyes slipped shut, his lashes quivering, his lips parting faintly as if on the verge of confession.

And right then, staring at those soft, pale pink lips, a sudden madness seized Wei Wuxian’s senses. As if possessed by a reckless, unholy impulse, he leaned down and pressed his mouth squarely against Lan Wangji’s.

And before pulling back, he parted his lips and gave them a teasing, lingering lick.

Both sets of eyes snapped wide open in absolute shock.

A heartbeat later, Lan Wangji’s hand shot up.

A jolt of pure adrenaline shattered Wei Wuxian’s daze, cold sweat drenching his spine. He's going to obliterate me! Assuming a lethal palm strike was about to blast his internal organs across the walls, Wei Wuxian threw himself off the mattress in a desperate, undignified roll.

He scrambled to his feet and whipped around—only to freeze.

Lan Wangji had slammed his own palm squarely against his own forehead.

Having knocked himself cold with a single concussive blow, the Second Young Master Lan collapsed backward, sprawling flat across the daybed in dead silence.

The room fell entirely still. Lan Wangji lay passed out on the mattress, while Wei Wuxian sat dazed on the cold floorboards. A gust of night air swept through the propped-open window, chilling his damp spine and shocking his racing mind back to reality.

He dragged himself upright, shoved the barricading table away from the door, and slumped into a chair.

After staring blankly into space for a long while, he leaned down and began aggressively gnawing at the stubborn knots cinched around his wrists. Teeth working relentlessly, he finally managed to tear through the seven or eight tangled knots Lan Wangji had mashed together.

Free at last, his hand instinctively reached out to pour a cup of wine to soothe his fried nerves. Lifting the porcelain to his mouth, he tipped it back—only to taste pure air. Glancing down, the cup was bone-dry. He’d drained the jar long before this circus started; his scrambled brain hadn't even registered that he’d just mimed pouring an empty jug.

Setting the cup down, Wei Wuxian scrubbed his face with both hands. Drink what? You’ve had way too much already tonight.

Glancing sideways past the folding screen, his eyes caught the peaceful, motionless figure sprawled across the daybed.

...I really took it too far, he thought, guilt prickling under his skin. Lan Zhan is an upright, dignified gentleman. Even if he’s blitzed out of his mind, even if he won't remember a single scrap tomorrow... treating him like that, crossing those lines... it’s dreadfully disrespectful.

Yet the moment the memory of that "disrespect" flashed through his mind, Wei Wuxian's fingers drifted up on pure instinct, lightly brushing against his own lips.

He picked up the wrinkled forehead ribbon, carefully smoothing out every crease and fold. Creeping over to the bed, he placed the pristine silk neatly beside the pillow, using every ounce of willpower to keep his eyes pinned away from Lan Wangji’s face. Dropping into a crouch, he slipped the man's white boots off and arranged his limbs into the rigid, pristine sleeping posture of the Gusu Lan clan.

Chores finished, Wei Wuxian slid down the side of the bed frame, resting his back against the timber as he stared into the dark.

A storm of chaotic, tangled thoughts churned through his skull, until finally, one single conclusion emerged with crystal clarity:

Never, under any circumstances, let Lan Zhan touch alcohol again. If he pulls this routine with anyone else, the cultivation world is going to burn.
